meta.note: Rating ladder. Each item names the lowest tier where it unlocks. Items repeat in higher tiers only when something changes.

tiers.label: 0% (service-connected, non-compensable)
tiers.intro: A 0% rating is still a win. It means VA agrees the condition is connected to service. No monthly pay, but doors open.

items.name: VA health care enrollment
items.detail: Free care for the 0% condition itself. Priority group 5, 7, or 8 by income for other care (group 6 if the 0% is compensable).

items.name: Commissary, exchange, and MWR access
items.detail: Any service-connected rating qualifies. Get a VHIC marked SERVICE CONNECTED.

items.name: 10-point federal hiring preference (XP)
items.detail: Any present service-connected disability, even 0%. Attach SF-15 and your VA letter.

items.name: A primary for secondary claims
items.detail: A 0% condition can be the cause of a later, higher-rated secondary condition.

items.name: Travel pay for service-connected care
items.detail: Mileage reimbursement for appointments treating the service-connected condition.

items.name: SMC-K possible
items.detail: Loss of use of a creative organ (for example erectile dysfunction) at 0% still earns the SMC-K add-on.

items.name: State benefits at 'any rating'
items.detail: Some states grant plates, park passes, or hiring points at any service-connected rating.

tiers.label: 10% to 20%
tiers.intro: Monthly pay begins, copays mostly end, and the funding fee waiver alone can be worth thousands.

items.name: Monthly compensation
items.detail: $180.42 at 10%, $356.66 at 20% (effective Dec 1, 2025). Tax-free.

items.name: No VA inpatient or outpatient copays
items.detail: Priority group 3. Medication copays still apply for non-service-connected conditions unless income is low.

items.name: VA home loan funding fee waived
items.detail: Anyone receiving compensation is exempt. Often $5,000 to $15,000 saved.

items.name: 10-point preference CP (10% to 29%)
items.detail: Compensable disability preference for federal jobs.

items.name: Chapter 31 VR&E at 10% with a serious employment handicap
items.detail: Training, degrees, tools, with a monthly allowance.

items.name: CRSC possible for retirees
items.detail: Combat-related conditions at 10%+ can qualify retirees for tax-free CRSC.

tiers.label: 30% to 40%
tiers.intro: Dependents start to count, travel pay opens for all VA appointments, and most veterans here should check for missing secondaries.

items.name: Extra pay for spouse, children, parents
items.detail: File 21-686c (and 21-674 for school-age kids) within one year to get back pay.

items.name: Travel pay for any VA appointment
items.detail: 41.5 cents a mile, small deductible.

items.name: Priority group 2
items.detail: No care copays. Medication copays may still apply.

items.name: 10-point preference CPS and the 30% noncompetitive authority
items.detail: Agencies can hire you directly at any grade.

items.name: Chapter 31 VR&E at 20%+ with an employment handicap
items.detail: The usual VR&E door.

items.name: TDIU math starts here
items.detail: A 40% condition is one half of the 70/40 TDIU test.

tiers.label: 50% to 60%
tiers.intro: All VA health care copays end at 50%. Retirees get CRDP. Many states open plates and passes at 50%.

items.name: Priority group 1: no copays at all
items.detail: No care copays and no medication copays for anything.

items.name: CRDP for 20-year retirees
items.detail: Retired pay restored at 50%+. Automatic.

items.name: TDIU with a single 60%
items.detail: One condition at 60% meets the schedular threshold if you cannot work.

items.name: HISA home alteration grant at 50%
items.detail: $6,800 lifetime for needed home changes, even for non-service-connected needs, with a single 50%+ rating.

items.name: State benefits at 50%
items.detail: Colorado: free DV plates and ownership tax exemption, free lifetime fishing and small game license, free Independence state parks pass.

tiers.label: 70% to 90%
tiers.intro: Caregiver stipends and TDIU become real options. At 80%+, small claims stop moving the needle; aim for 100% or TDIU the right way.

items.name: PCAFC caregiver program at 70%
items.detail: Monthly stipend, CHAMPVA for the caregiver, respite, training.

items.name: TDIU with 70% combined and one 40%
items.detail: Paid at the 100% rate if you cannot hold substantially gainful work.

items.name: Many state property tax exemptions start here
items.detail: Varies by state. Check yours.

items.name: Plan the path to 100%
items.detail: At 80%, a new 10% does almost nothing. A 30%+ condition in a new body system, or a 70% mental health rating, is the usual move.

tiers.label: 100% (schedular or TDIU)
tiers.intro: The full monthly rate, VA dental, and extra dependent pay. SMC is the only thing left to claim.

items.name: Full rate: $3,938.58 a month, veteran alone
items.detail: Higher with dependents. Effective Dec 1, 2025.

items.name: VA dental care, Class IV
items.detail: Any needed dental care at 100% schedular or TDIU. Temporary 100% does not count.

items.name: Special Monthly Compensation
items.detail: SMC-S if you also have a separate 60% or are housebound; aid and attendance if you need daily help.

items.name: Highest dependent add-ons
items.detail: Spouse +$219.59, each school-age child +$352.45.

items.name: Commissary access already included
items.detail: 100% and TDIU veterans had access before the 2020 expansion.

items.name: Ask about P&T
items.detail: If your conditions will not improve, request the permanent finding. It unlocks the next tier.

tiers.label: 100% Permanent and Total (P&T)
tiers.intro: The family tier. Health coverage and school money for your spouse and kids, and the top tier of nearly every state benefit.

items.name: CHAMPVA for spouse and children
items.detail: VA-paid health coverage. Form 10-10d.

items.name: Chapter 35 education for spouse and children
items.detail: $1,621 a month full time (Oct 1, 2026), 36 months each. Form 22-5490.

items.name: State property tax exemptions at the top tier
items.detail: Colorado: 50% of the first $200,000 of home value, also for TDIU since 2025.

items.name: No routine re-examinations
items.detail: VA does not schedule future exams on P&T ratings unless you file something.

items.name: Expedited Social Security disability processing
items.detail: Write 'Veteran 100% P&T' in remarks and attach your letter.

items.name: Survivor protections
items.detail: If you die of a service-connected condition, or after 10 years at P&T, survivors may qualify for DIC. Form 21P-534EZ.
